meta.title: Tokendial — your AI coding limits on a dial, before they stop you
meta.description: Made for vibecoders: a dock on the edge of your screen with one dial per AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and more). It warns you before a window resets, when a limit hits, and when an agent is waiting for your yes. Free and open source, macOS and Windows.
hero.eyebrow: Made for vibecoders · macOS · Windows · free
hero.title: Don't let a usage limit kill the vibe.
hero.lead: You build with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot… and the only way to find out you are running out is when they stop. Tokendial puts a dial on the edge of your screen for each one, warns you before a window resets, and pings you when an agent is waiting for a yes.
hero.note: Free · No account · No terminal needed to set it up

why.title: Built for how you actually code now
why.lead: Several assistants, several subscriptions, several limits that reset on their own schedule. Nobody should keep that in their head while shipping.
why.1.title: See all your tools at once
why.1.body: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Antigravity, GLM, Grok, OpenCode. One glance tells you which one still has room for the next prompt.
why.2.title: Know when to switch or wait
why.2.body: Every dial shows the window that matters and when it resets. At 80 % you move the task to another tool, or take the break until it comes back.
why.3.title: Never miss the agent asking for a yes
why.3.body: When Claude Code stops for a permission and you are in another window, its mark beats on the dock and a banner tells you who is waiting and for what.
how.title: Zero setup. It reads what your tools already know
how.1.title: It finds your tools
how.1.body: If you have signed in to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, that sign-in is already on your computer. Tokendial reads it there, read-only, and never writes, refreshes or copies it.
how.2.title: It asks the vendor, not you
how.2.body: The same usage numbers each tool's own status bar shows, fetched from the vendor once a minute while you work and every five when you rest.
how.3.title: It shows a dial, not a spreadsheet
how.3.body: Green, amber, red. Hover for every window, its reset time and the sessions running. Ignore it the rest of the time.
providers.title: Nine assistants, one dial each
providers.lead: Every provider is opt-in and can be switched off at any time. Where a vendor publishes no ceiling, the dial shows the bare count and says so.
providers.claude.detail: Session and weekly limits, per model
alerts.title: Notifications when they help, silence when you are already looking
alerts.lead: Native notifications, or Tokendial's own banners in your system accent color when Do Not Disturb swallows the rest. Quiet while the dock is open under your cursor. At most one per provider per minute.
alerts.1.title: Threshold
alerts.1.body: Crossing 50, 80 or 95 % of a window, once per window.
alerts.2.title: Reset soon
alerts.2.body: Ten minutes before a window you have leaned on resets, and again when a limit lifts so you can get back to it.
alerts.3.title: Waiting for you
alerts.3.body: An agent has waited on your answer for 20 seconds. Its mark beats on the dock until you come back.
alerts.4.title: Limit reached
alerts.4.body: A window hit 100 % or the vendor blocked you, with the hour it lifts.
dock.title: Any edge, any look
dock.1.title: Four positions
dock.1.body: Top or bottom as a row, left or right as a column. It expands towards the screen and stays out of the way otherwise.
dock.2.title: Dark and light
dock.2.body: Follows Windows or macOS, or pick one. Dials, cards and banners are drawn from the same tokens.
dock.3.title: Six languages
dock.3.body: English, British English, Spanish, French, German and Arabic, right-to-left included, switchable without restarting.
install.title: Don't have the tool yet? One click.
install.lead: Want to try Codex or Grok but never touched a terminal? A provider whose tool is missing offers Install → Sign in → Ready. Tokendial shows the vendor's official command, you press Run, it walks you through the sign-in, and the dial is there when you are done.
install.1: Shows the exact command and where the vendor documents it, before anything runs
install.2: Runs it in a visible terminal, never elevated, never hidden
install.3: Chains the tool's own sign-in and connects the dial the moment it lands
security.title: Your keys never leave your machine
security.1: No account, no telemetry, no crash reports. The only request that is not to a provider is one a day to GitHub Releases to learn whether a newer version exists, and Settings can switch it off.
security.2: Credentials are read where their tool keeps them and are never stored, written or refreshed.
security.3: Every endpoint host is a constant in the code and in the public specs; redirects are refused.
security.4: Logs carry status codes and Tokendial's own messages, never headers, bodies or URLs.
cta.title: Keep the vibe going.
cta.lead: Free and open source, Windows and macOS, built from one shared specification.
